sections.heading: Urgent correction criteria
sections.text: Use the urgent correction route only when the current instruction can cause an immediate service interruption or directs a user to perform an action known to be incorrect. Record the defective instruction, supporting evidence, affected audience, and consequence of waiting. A preferred publication date or a late request is not sufficient evidence of urgency.

sections.heading: Shorter notice authorization
sections.text: The document owner and an affected process representative may jointly authorize an effective date with less than five working days of notice. Both roles must record their decisions before publication. The controller sends a direct notice to the affected audience before the corrected instruction takes effect. The exception does not waive independent review or the comparison of published and reviewed content.

sections.heading: Follow-up and evidence
sections.text: Within two working days after an urgent publication, the document owner checks that affected teams received the notice and records any unresolved action. Keep the request, reviewed revision, review decisions, publication record, distribution evidence, and exception together. A comparison screenshot can illustrate a change but cannot establish review completion or publication authority.
